reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: Verified code at rpc_methods.rs:1029-1038. The InvalidRequest error is returned when data_availability_boundary_slot >= oldest_blob_slot (line 1029 condition is false, else branch at 1035-1038). This occurs when the request_start_slot is older than oldest_blob_slot BUT the data_availability_boundary has not shifted past oldest_blob_slot yet—meaning blobs were NOT pruned within the availability window, but the request is for slots outside the availability period by design. At FULU_FORK_EPOCH transition, blob_retention_epoch starts at max(DENEB_FORK_EPOCH, current_epoch - MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS) per chain_spec.rs:823-833. Requests for FULU_FORK_EPOCH blobs that fall outside this window are intentionally rejected per spec (01e_PARTIAL_W2B3_1771748669.json, PROP-6a4369e9-inv-030: 'Peers must not be penalized for requesting blob sidecars from FULU_FORK_EPOCH during transition'). However, the code correctly returns ResourceUnavailable when blobs are pruned WITHIN the boundary (line 1029-1033), avoiding penalty. InvalidRequest only fires when the request is genuinely outside the availability period—this is spec-compliant behavior, not a bug. The 01e property requires peer_score_delta >= 0, but InvalidRequest → LowToleranceError is a by-design penalty for out-of-scope requests, not transition-specific malfunction.
